---
title: "camdl"
subtitle: "Compartmental Model Description Language"
toc: false
---

camdl describes stochastic compartmental models. A `.camdl` file says what the
compartments are, how individuals move between them and how fast; the compiler
expands it to a flat intermediate representation that a Rust runtime simulates
and fits to data.

Most guides and reference pages here are the same text the binary carries:
`camdl docs <topic>` prints them offline, matched to the installed version.
The tutorials are website-only, because they show the real output of each
command, regenerated from the current code every time the site is built.

<!-- figure: architecture, caption: camdl's architecture reshapes how responsibility is split between the modeler and camdl's developers. A researcher needs only to define the model's structure and prior assumptions, not its implementation or inference; camdl's responsibility is to execute the declared model faithfully and exactly. A trajectory inconsistent with the declared semantics is therefore a bug report against camdl, never the researcher's fault, and implementation risk moves from many privately maintained code bases to one audited, tested, externally validated one. -->
